screening_decisions.reason: This is a randomized controlled trial involving adults with HF (mean age 75±8 years). The intervention consists of a tablet computer delivering HF information and lifestyle advice, which qualifies as mHealth-delivered education (via mobile device). The control group receives standard HF information only (usual care). All criteria are met.

This is a three-group parallel-randomized trial with stable HF adults (mean age 66.8±11.0 years). One intervention group receives the 'heartfailurematters.org' website, which is an internet/web-based education program qualifying as mHealth-delivered education, compared to usual care. The study meets all inclusion criteria.

This is a randomized controlled trial of patients with HF. The intervention is a web-based self-care intervention, which qualifies as mHealth-delivered education (internet/web-based). The control group receives usual care. The study involves adults with HF and meets all criteria.

This is a randomized clinical trial of HF patients. The intervention group receives SMS follow-up, which qualifies as mHealth-delivered education (SMS messages). The comparison groups receive telephone and regular follow-up (considered usual care variants). The study involves adults with HF and meets criteria.

While this is an RCT of adults with CHF, the education intervention is delivered through multiple modalities: nurse-led face-to-face counseling, computer-based education, and written teaching materials. The education is not solely mHealth-delivered as required by the criteria (which specifies mHealth-delivered education such as internet/web-based, apps, SMS, or social media).

This is an RCT of adults with HF, but the intervention combines nurse-led counseling, computer-based education, and written materials. The education component is not exclusively mHealth-delivered; it includes face-to-face counseling and written materials, which falls outside the specified mHealth delivery methods (internet/web-based, apps, SMS, social media).

This is an RCT of adults with CHF, but the intervention consists of a nurse-guided education program, facilitated telephone communication, and follow-up visits. The education is delivered by nurses, not via mHealth technologies. While telephone communication could be considered mHealth, it is used for communication rather than as the primary delivery mechanism for education content.

This is an RCT of hospitalized HF patients (mean age 60±14 years). The intervention is video education (VE) in addition to standard education. Video education can be considered mHealth-delivered when viewed on mobile devices, and given the review's focus on mHealth for self-care support, this intervention qualifies. The control group receives standard education only. When in doubt, we include conservatively.

This is a pilot study (not an RCT) focusing on system usability and user experiences. There is no comparison between an mHealth education intervention and usual care. The study does not meet the RCT requirement for inclusion.

This study analyzes recruitment challenges for an mHealth intervention but is not an RCT comparing outcomes. It lacks the required randomized controlled trial design comparing mHealth-delivered education versus usual care.

While this is an RCT of adults with CHF using a web-based device, the primary focus is on medication compliance monitoring rather than education delivery. The intervention is described as a 'self-care and medication compliance device' with outcomes measuring compliance, not education. It does not clearly represent mHealth-delivered education as specified in the criteria.

This is a proof of concept paper using exploratory inquiry and field study methods, not a randomized controlled trial. It does not compare an mHealth education intervention against usual care in an RCT design, which is required for inclusion.

This is a descriptive survey design assessing usability and user confidence, not an RCT. There is no comparison of an mHealth education intervention versus usual care on clinical outcomes. It lacks the required RCT design.

This is a study protocol document, not a completed RCT with results. While it describes a planned RCT, screening criteria require actual completed studies to assess whether they meet the inclusion criteria based on reported methods and results.

This is an RCT of adults with HF, but the PCDM intervention is a multifaceted collaborative care approach including home telemonitoring, self-management support, and depression treatment. While it contains mHealth elements (telemonitoring), it is not purely mHealth-delivered education as specified; it includes multiple components beyond education delivery via mobile/wireless technologies.

This article describes the rationale and design of the CASA trial but does not present results from a completed RCT. It is a protocol/paper about study design, not empirical evidence from a completed trial that can be screened against the inclusion criteria.

This is a six-month randomized field experiment (RCT) comparing a technology-enhanced practice (TEP) model including the HeartCareII website (a web-based resource) against usual care delivered by home care nurses. The web resource qualifies as mHealth-delivered education (internet/web-based). The study involves HF patients and meets all criteria: RCT, adults with HF, mHealth-delivered education vs. usual care.

Intervention is motivational interviewing via telephone, not mHealth-delivered education as defined (internet/web-based programs, apps, SMS, social media). Telephone follow-up is not explicitly listed as an mHealth education modality, and the intervention focuses on counseling rather than structured education.

Population consists of Indigenous people with or at high risk of CVD, not specifically heart failure. Intervention uses tablet application during education sessions but is not purely mHealth-delivered education; it is a blended approach with nurse-led sessions.

RCT of a mobile phone-assisted case management program in minority HF patients. Intervention involves mobile phone technology to support self-care efficacy, knowledge, and behavior, which aligns with mHealth-delivered education components. Compares to usual care.
Intervention is telehomecare focused on monitoring clinical indices and detecting cardiac status changes, not explicitly on delivering education. No clear education component described.

Study investigates telehealth influence on self-management but does not specify an RCT design (uses repeated measures). Intervention is a telehealth system for data transmission, likely monitoring-focused, not explicitly education.

While RCT and HF population, intervention uses Health Buddy telehealth system for monitoring and reminders; not clearly structured mHealth-delivered education (e.g., no internet/web-based programs, apps, SMS, social media described as education delivery).

RCT comparing internet-based synchronized face-to-face video education sessions (via Vidyo) plus physical activity feedback (Fitbit) to usual care (handout, exercise routine, Fitbit only). Intervention delivers education via internet-based video, fitting mHealth-delivered education definition.
Quasi-experimental design, not an RCT. Fails the randomized controlled trial requirement.
Feasibility study of a web-based program without a control group; not an RCT. No comparison to usual care.
Intervention consists of e-mail reminders to nurses (provider-focused), not mHealth-delivered education to patients. Does not meet the criterion of patient education via mHealth.
Feasibility study of an HF app without a control group; not an RCT. No comparison to usual care.

Multi-center RCT of patients with chronic HF (and/or coronary artery disease). Intervention adds an internet-based telerehabilitation program (likely includes education as a core component of cardiac rehab) to standard cardiac rehabilitation, compared to standard cardiac rehabilitation alone. Delivers education via internet-based telerehabilitation, fitting mHealth-delivered education.
Systematic literature review, not an RCT. Does not meet study design criterion.
RCT focuses on telemonitoring medication adherence with telephonic support; intervention is monitoring-focused, not explicitly education-delivered. No education component described.

While RCT and includes HF patients, intervention is a multifaceted telehealth intervention (not explicitly education-focused). Control group received usual care plus education, making the comparison unclear for mHealth-delivered education vs usual HF care.

Feasibility trial compares medication reminder systems (electronic pill box, smartphone app) with/without reminders. Intervention is reminder-focused, not education-delivered. No education component described.
RCT compares remote medication monitoring system (MedSentry) to usual care. Intervention is monitoring-focused, not explicitly education-delivered. No education component described.

This is a review article about implantable and non-implantable devices for monitoring heart failure, not a randomized controlled trial comparing mHealth-delivered education versus usual care.

This is a cluster-randomized parallel groups trial involving patients with congestive heart failure (among other conditions). The intervention is individualized health coaching by telephony, which constitutes mHealth-delivered education/support compared to a control arm (usual care).

While this is a randomized trial in older adults with heart failure, the intervention is a telemonitoring system with telephone support, which is primarily monitoring rather than mHealth-delivered education as specified in the selection criteria.

This randomized study examines remote patient monitoring (live nursing visits and video-based nursing visits) versus live nursing visits only. The intervention focuses on monitoring rather than mHealth-delivered education.
This study uses a community-based participatory research approach with focus groups, not a randomized controlled trial. It does not meet the RCT requirement.

This is a randomized comparative effectiveness trial involving heart failure patients. The intervention ('mobile health+CarePartner') includes automated self-care support calls and email summaries/suggestions for self-care assistance, which constitutes mHealth-delivered education compared to standard mHealth support.

This is a study protocol for an RCT, not reporting results of a completed trial. The intervention is an IVR-enhanced care transition intervention, which is not primarily focused on education as specified in the selection criteria.

While this is a pragmatic randomized trial in patients with CHF/COPD, the E-Coach intervention is a technology-supported care transition support program focused on reducing rehospitalization, not primarily mHealth-delivered education.

This randomized controlled trial provided heart failure patients with access to a web-based electronic medical record that included an educational guide and messaging system. This constitutes mHealth-delivered education (web-based) versus usual care.

While this is a cluster-randomized clinical trial using a Web-based tool, the population is not specifically limited to heart failure patients (includes coronary heart disease, stroke, diabetes, etc.), and the intervention focuses on preventive messages for multiple diseases rather than HF-specific education.

This appears to be an observational cohort study (not an RCT) examining the relationship between HbA1c and mortality in patients with T2DM and incident CHF. It does not compare mHealth-delivered education versus usual care.
This study uses a qualitative focus group design, not a randomized controlled trial. It does not meet the RCT requirement.

This study uses semi-structured interviews to gather perceptions and experiences, not a randomized controlled trial. It examines a mobile phone-based telemonitoring system, which is primarily monitoring rather than education.

While this is an RCT in heart failure patients using a mobile phone-based telemonitoring system, the intervention focuses on monitoring (weight, BP, ECG, symptom questions) with some instructional components. It is not primarily an mHealth-delivered education intervention as specified in the selection criteria.

This is a study protocol for an RCT, not reporting results of a completed trial. The intervention is a smartphone-based telemonitoring system, which is primarily monitoring rather than mHealth-delivered education.
This paper describes the design and rationale of an ongoing RCT, not reporting results of a completed trial. It does not provide outcome data for screening.

While this is an RCT in heart failure patients comparing computer-based education plus standard education versus standard education only, the intervention is computer-based but not specifically delivered via mobile/web-based technologies for smartphones/tablets/apps, SMS, or social media as specified in the selection criteria.
This appears to be a review or discussion of remote monitoring benefits, not a randomized controlled trial reporting results. It does not meet the RCT requirement for inclusion.

This is a study protocol for an RCT, not reporting results of a completed trial. While it involves motivational interviewing for HF patients, it does not specify that the intervention is delivered via mHealth technologies (smartphones/tablets/apps, SMS, social media) as required.
While this is a 12-month pilot trial with random assignment in patients with CHF/COPD, the intervention is home telemonitoring, which is primarily monitoring rather than mHealth-delivered education.

This is a randomized controlled trial in heart failure patients, but the intervention consists of a DVD and booklet (Living with Heart Failure). This is not delivered via mHealth technologies (internet/web-based for smartphones/tablets/apps, SMS, or social media) as specified in the selection criteria.

This randomized trial compares integrated management (using a handheld PDA + daily contact with monitoring centre) versus usual care. While it has some supportive elements, the intervention is primarily telemonitoring/telecare rather than mHealth-delivered education.
This study uses a questionnaire-based survey to assess consumer information materials, not a randomized controlled trial. It does not meet the RCT requirement.

This prospective study compared a Web-based educational and HF management program for older HF patients (60+ years) versus an age- and sex-matched control group receiving usual HF care. The intervention is a web-based educational program, which constitutes mHealth-delivered education as specified in the selection criteria.
This is a retrospective study examining the effects of remote monitoring in heart failure patients, not a randomized controlled trial. It does not meet the RCT requirement.
This study uses a case-matched design via retrospective chart reviews to analyze costs of remote monitoring services, not a randomized controlled trial. It does not meet the RCT requirement.
This is a feasibility study enrolling healthy volunteers, not patients with heart failure, and is not a randomized controlled trial. It does not meet the population or study design requirements.
This paper describes the rationale and design of an RCT, not reporting results of a completed trial. It does not provide outcome data for screening.

This research aims to develop and test a taxonomy of behavior change techniques. It is not a randomized controlled trial involving heart failure patients or comparing mHealth-delivered education versus usual care.

This analysis uses registry data from hospitals to examine characteristics of nonadherent HF patients. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not compare mHealth-delivered education versus usual care.

While this is an RCT in patients with systolic heart failure comparing a nurse-coordinated disease management program (including telephone-based monitoring and education) versus usual care, the intervention is a multi-component disease management program rather than primarily mHealth-delivered education as specified in the selection criteria.

This is a methodological paper describing a system for grading evidence and recommendations. It is not a randomized controlled trial involving heart failure patients or comparing mHealth-delivered education versus usual care.

This randomized trial compared a 'teach to goal' educational and behavioral support program (telephone education and counselling with reinforcement) versus a brief educational intervention in heart failure patients. The telephone-delivered education constitutes mHealth-delivered education as specified in the selection criteria.
